posts.title: Tooltips that follow their anchor
posts.markdown:
A tooltip should stay attached to the thing it explains, even when the page scrolls. Modern CSS can do most of this on its own.

## The idea

Anchor the tooltip to its trigger and let the browser keep them together.

```css
.tip { position-anchor: --trigger; top: anchor(bottom); }
```

posts.title: Designing shadows that feel real
posts.markdown:
Real shadows are soft, layered and a little coloured. One flat grey box-shadow is none of those things.

## Layer them

```css
box-shadow: 0 1px 2px hsl(220 40% 20% / .1), 0 8px 24px hsl(220 40% 20% / .12);
```

posts.title: The humble transform-origin
posts.markdown:
Every rotation and scale happens around a point. Move the point and the whole animation changes character.

Try a card that grows from its corner instead of its centre: it suddenly feels like it is unfolding.

posts.title: An interactive guide to CSS transitions
posts.markdown:
Transitions are the smallest piece of animation on the web and the one used most. Duration, easing and delay are all you need to know to start.

## Easing is the personality

Linear feels mechanical. Ease-out feels responsive. A little overshoot feels playful.

posts.title: Why your z-index doesn't work
posts.markdown:
Nine times out of ten, the element is in a different stacking context from the one you think. A transform, an opacity or a filter on a parent quietly starts a new one.

posts.title: A gentle introduction to SVG paths
posts.markdown:
A path is a list of drawing instructions: move here, draw a line there, curve over to this point.

```svg
<path d="M 10 80 Q 95 10 180 80" />
```
